# Mainnet Deployments
Source: https://docs.kuru.io/deployments/mainnet

Contract addresses, tokens, market parameters, and price sources for Monad mainnet.

This reference includes the current AccountCore implementation and the addresses and parameters from the [15 October 2026 mainnet deployment record](https://gist.github.com/devblixt/0093a81e9fc21b6c96e74ac3d3eb08e9). The [testnet reference](/deployments/testnet) lists the separate test deployment. Check live onchain state before sending transactions because administrative parameters can change.

## Network

| Setting | Value |
| - | - |
| Network | Monad mainnet |
| Chain ID | `143` |
| RPC | `https://rpc.monad.xyz` |
| Explorer | [https://monadvision.com](https://monadvision.com) |
| Gas token | MON, 18 decimals |

## Contract addresses

| Component | Address | Purpose |
| - | - | - |
| AccountCore proxy | `0x264123a9B96Cc1193944cC25C188f1bD3dFa670e` | ERC-20 spender; custody, deposits, withdrawals, accounts and signers |
| WithdrawalLimiter proxy | `0xF059F4AAb49Bd3AFB62134145EeAF38Fe103F0eA` | Withdrawal budget and token-to-price-source mappings |
| SpotRouter proxy | `0xBdDF3556701B7ECca5d69416CFfd7F86D37E52b3` | Market registration and administration |
| KuruTradingWallet implementation | `0xa478b5a38aabDf8b31f0ec7443a274162214Cd18` | EIP-7702 delegation target |

Approve and deposit tokens into **AccountCore**. Send direct trading calls to the **market address** below. Signed trading-wallet actions execute through the delegated EOA; KuruTradingWallet is its EIP-7702 implementation.

| EWYx/USDC | `0xED3727e833200c849fbd18e15eD0D091c9B0F3aF` |

### Market parameters

| Market | sizePrecision | pricePrecision | tickSize | passiveSpreadTicks | Passive spread (\$) |
| - | - | - | - | - | - |
| MON/USDC | 10000000000 | 100000000 | 100 | 100 | \$0.0001 |
| WETH/USDC | 10000000000 | 10000 | 100 | 100 | \$1 |
| cbBTC/USDC | 100000000 | 1000 | 100 | 100 | \$10 |
| XAUt0/USDC | 1000000 | 10000 | 100 | 100 | \$1 |
| NVDAx/USDC | 10000000000 | 10000 | 100 | 10 | \$0.1 |
| SPYx/USDC | 10000000000 | 10000 | 100 | 10 | \$0.1 |

| TSLAx/USDC | 10000000000 | 10000 | 100 | 10 | \$0.1 |
| EWYx/USDC | 10000000000 | 10000 | 100 | 10 | \$0.1 |

Dollar spreads assume USDC = \$1. Passive spread is a configured market parameter, not the live bid/ask spread. Order quantity uses `sizePrecision`; order price uses `pricePrecision` and must align to `tickSize`. Deposits and withdrawals use token decimals.

### Fees and order limits

| Parameter | Value | Contract value |
| - | - | - |
| Default maker fee | 1 bps | `defaultSpotMakerFeePps = 1000` |
| Default taker fee | 2 bps | `defaultSpotTakerFeePps = 2000` |
| Market maker/taker caps | 100 bps each | `makerFeePps = 100000`, `takerFeePps = 100000` |
| Minimum quote notional | 10 USDC | `minQuoteNotional = 10000000` |
| Maximum quote notional | 5,000,000 USDC | `maxQuoteNotional = 5000000000000` |

AccountCore default fees are enabled. The 100-bps market values cap the applicable fees; the default trading rates are **1 bps maker / 2 bps taker**. Account-specific tiers and builder fees can affect the final charge. Fee rates use a denominator of `10000000`. See [OrderBook](/contracts/order-book) for fee calculation.

The 10-USDC minimum is inclusive and applies to order admission before fees, not to each partial fill.

## Tokens

WETH uses ETH/USD and cbBTC uses BTC/USD at 1:1. The maximum age is the contract acceptance limit, not a publication schedule. Stale observations can prevent deposits or withdrawals until fresh prices become available.

<Accordion title="Implementation and authority addresses">
  | Component | Address | Purpose |
  | - | - | - |
  | ProtocolAuthority | `0x15db88bAc73D856B3ca53683F82058826A3b6E8f` | Governance, ops and emergency role registry |
  | KeeperAuthority | `0xbc36eC07800150489f9ED0f86a2d3E27Ca36980e` | Trading-wallet keeper authorization |
  | AccountCore implementation | `0xB52deBaD718730eE0a4C12C28E70d346dbCc9E5B` | Implementation behind AccountCore proxy |
  | WithdrawalLimiter implementation | `0x64E621868318a68DfD1F374EC75bd3Cd5B72b349` | Implementation behind limiter proxy |
  | SpotRouter implementation | `0x70DD3E2F643A187D34eD54a58AFEdF717464FCD9` | Implementation behind router proxy |
  | Shared OrderBook implementation | `0x38e7620A96E79A1d2B4439c68141203d757D69E6` | Implementation behind all nine market proxies |
  | KuruFastLanePeriphery | `0x86400a84364e167b933b18e1484369679cDbEcA9` | FastLane execution adapter for the current trading wallet |

  Use the AccountCore, WithdrawalLimiter and SpotRouter proxies above for contract calls. Their implementation addresses identify the code behind those proxies.
</Accordion>


# AccountCore methods

| Method | Signed authority | Effect |
| - | - | - |
| [Revoke signer](/api/relay/reference/revoke-account-signer) | Root owner or live ADMIN | Revoke signer and advance the root authorization epoch |
| [Create subaccount](/api/relay/reference/create-subaccount) | Root owner or live ADMIN/TRADE | Create the next child sequence; epoch unchanged |

The frontend trading wallet supplies the Relay JWT, but **the JWT identity does not need to equal the AccountCore `authorizer`, owner/root owner, or signer being revoked**. JWT identity controls service admission and sponsorship only. A separate owner or authorized EOA signs the AccountCore EIP-712 request using domain `KuruAccountCore`, version `1`, and the configured AccountCore proxy as verifying contract. These two methods accept canonical 65-byte or ERC-2098 64-byte EOA signatures; they do not add ERC-1271 support. The older signer-grant onboarding route keeps its distinct JWT-to-new-signer binding.

Read `nonce` or `authNonce` from AccountCore: these are uint256 root authorization epochs, **not** millisecond trading nonces. For subaccount creation, use the next nonzero uint16 `subaccountSeq`, wait for inclusion, then read again before creating another child. A pending creation is not assumed to have changed `latest` state for the next simulation.

## Immediate errors and recovery

* `OPERATIONAL_SIMULATION_REVERTED` (HTTP 400) means the exact simulation explicitly reverted. No transaction was signed or broadcast; correct the state or request before retrying.
* `POLICY_DECLINED` (HTTP 403) can mean the buffered estimate exceeded the method's gas cap. No gas amount is silently clipped.
* `GAS_POLICY_UNAVAILABLE` (HTTP 503, retryable) covers estimator saturation, timeouts, malformed estimates, and transient provider failures. A generic RPC failure is not a proven contract revert.
* `INTERNAL_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` (HTTP 504) can mean the caller's deadline elapsed during estimation. Reconcile any ambiguous submission before retrying.

After a successful `BROADCAST`, use the usual [Relay outcomes and recovery](/api/relay/errors) rules. A simulation is not an execution guarantee: balances, orders, permissions, and nonce state may change before inclusion. Do not blindly resubmit a FOK or account-administration operation after a lost reply.

# Kuru main — Monad mainnet deployment reference

Deployed **15 October 2026** (Asia/Kolkata). This reference covers the new Spot protocol: AccountCore custody, router, withdrawal limiter, trading-wallet periphery, ten price sources and **nine ACTIVE markets**.

**Default trading fees: 1 bps maker / 2 bps taker.** All nine markets use USDC as quote, a **10 USDC minimum** and **5,000,000 USDC maximum** quote notional. USDT/USDC is excluded. KEEPER1 is publishing to the six new manual price sources.

Use the new addresses below. Account IDs, balances, orders and approvals were not migrated from the previous deployment.

## 1. Network and source identity

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Network | Monad mainnet |
| Chain ID | `143` (`0x8f`) |
| RPC | `https://rpc.monad.xyz` |
| Explorer | https://monadvision.com |
| Native currency | MON, 18 decimals |
| Native-token sentinel | `0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000` |
| Source branch / revision | `main` / `bcf0b7c8e54722abdf50ddd43d36262725efa41f` |
| Compiler | Solidity `0.8.37+commit.f401782d` |
| Build settings | Optimizer enabled, 10,000 runs, via IR, EVM **Osaka** |
| Metadata | IPFS bytecode hash; CBOR enabled |
| Foundry | `1.8.5`; network `monad`, hardfork `monad:MonadTen` |
| OpenZeppelin | `5.7.0`, commit `cab19933c33c2ad1d4c7a84864a3601dddfd16f3` |
| Solady | `0.1.26`, commit `acd959aa4bd04720d640bf4e6a5c71037510cc4b` |
| forge-std | `1.17.0`, commit `f3dae6e6ee381f25eb6a246f7da9b85c91a68219` (test/script tooling; not deployed) |

The compiler and library pins are the approved build overrides on top of the pinned main revision. An unmodified checkout of main may have different build pins. Live bytecode and metadata matched the deployment artifacts; 73 compiled source files matched their pinned Git commits. No public explorer/source verification was submitted for this deployment.

## 2. Contract addresses and call routing

Use **proxy addresses** for custody and trading.

| Component | Address | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AccountCore proxy | `0x264123a9B96Cc1193944cC25C188f1bD3dFa670e` | Custody, ERC-20 spender, deposits, withdrawals, accounts and signers |

| ProtocolAuthority | `0x15db88bAc73D856B3ca53683F82058826A3b6E8f` | Governance, ops and emergency roles |

| Shared OrderBook implementation | `0x38e7620A96E79A1d2B4439c68141203d757D69E6` | Code behind all nine market proxies |

**Trade directly against the market proxies in section 5.** Approve ERC-20 deposits to AccountCore `0x264123a9B96Cc1193944cC25C188f1bD3dFa670e`, then call its `deposit` function. A plain token transfer does not credit an account. Do not send funds to implementation addresses.

At block **113639762**, 148 connection checks passed: core/router/limiter bindings, all price-source core bindings, market registrations and implementation slots, authority links and trading-wallet dependencies. None of those protocol bindings point to an old deployment contract. The new core/router do not recognize the old markets. Token contracts, external Chainlink feeds and operator wallets are intentionally shared.

### Units for integration

- Limit-order `quantity` uses **sizePrecision units**: human base quantity = `quantity / sizePrecision`.
- Limit-order `price` uses **pricePrecision units**: human USDC/base = `price / pricePrecision`; encoded prices must respect `tickSize`.
- Raw base amount = `quantity * baseSizeMultiplier`, where `baseSizeMultiplier = 10^baseDecimals / sizePrecision`.
- Deposits, withdrawals and `swap` amounts use **raw token atoms**.
- Example: 1 MON is `10000000000` order-size units or `1000000000000000000` raw atoms. A MON limit price of 0.025 USDC is encoded as `2500000`.

## 7. Deposits, accounts and withdrawals


### Deposit and balance addresses

All operations below target the **AccountCore proxy** from section 2. Amounts are raw token atoms.

```solidity
deposit(address rootOwner, address token, uint256 amount) payable;
deposit(uint40 rootAccountId, address token, uint256 amount) payable;
withdraw(uint40 rootAccountId, address token, uint256 amount, address recipient);
rootAccountIdOf(address owner) view returns (uint40);
getBalance(uint40 accountId, address token) view returns (uint256);
getSpotReservedBalance(uint40 accountId, address token) view returns (uint256);
createSubaccount(address rootOwner) returns (uint40);
transferBetweenAccounts(uint40 fromAccountId, uint40 toAccountId, address token, uint256 amount);
```

For ERC-20 deposits, approve **AccountCore**, then call `deposit` with zero native value. The address overload creates the owner's root account if needed; the ID overload requires an existing root. For native MON, pass the zero-address token sentinel and set `msg.value = amount`; no ERC-20 approval is involved. A plain transfer to the contract is not a substitute for a credited deposit.

External deposits and withdrawals are **root-account only**. Fund children with `transferBetweenAccounts` within the same root and return funds to the root before withdrawing. Internal transfers do not create new deposit credit. Free balance and maker-reserved balance are separate; reserved funds must become free before withdrawal.

Ordinary withdrawals require the owner or an authorized WITHDRAW signer, sufficient free balance, a valid recipient, active protocol/releases, a fresh price and available global withdrawal capacity. The recipient is explicit and need not equal the owner. There is no withdrawal queue in this deployed path.

### Limiter configuration

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Global drip capacity | 0 (`capacityUsd18 = 0`) |
| Global drip refill | 0 (`ratePerSecondUsd18 = 0`) |
| Deposit-credit window | 86400 seconds (24 hours) |
| Withdrawal authority | Unset (zero address) |
| Withdrawal authority epoch | 1 |

The withdrawal budget is **shared across accounts and assets**. Deposits add USD-valued credit that expires after 24 hours, and ordinary withdrawals consume that credit. With drip capacity and refill both zero, there is no additional replenishing allowance when deposit credit is exhausted. Deposits and withdrawals use the fresh USD valuation at the time of each custody operation.

Read capacity on WithdrawalLimiter:

```solidity
previewWithdrawal(address token, uint256 amount)
    view returns (uint256 requiredUsd36, uint256 availableUsd36, bool withinLimit);
struct CapacityState {
    uint256 depositCreditUsd36;
    uint256 dripCreditUsd36;
    uint256 availableUsd36;
}
getCapacityState() view returns (CapacityState memory);
priceSource(address token) view returns (address);
```

Capacity outputs are **USD36**; divide by `10^36` for human USD. Configuration and source prices use USD18. `previewWithdrawal` does not establish caller authorization, free balance or release eligibility.

### Authority-approved payouts

The `fulfillApprovedWithdrawal` path exists in the implementation, but the mainnet withdrawal authority is currently unset. Do not carry the testnet executor address or signatures into this deployment.

The AccountCore EIP-712 domain uses `name = "KuruAccountCore"`, `version = "1"`, `chainId = 143`, and `verifyingContract = 0x264123a9B96Cc1193944cC25C188f1bD3dFa670e`. If an authority is configured later, read `approvedWithdrawalNonces(account)` and `withdrawalAuthorityEpoch()` immediately before signing and use the exact deployed struct schema.

Account IDs are deployment-specific. Resolve a user's root with `rootAccountIdOf(owner)` instead of reusing testnet account IDs.

## 8. Trading, delegated wallets and keepers


For direct trading, call the desired **OrderBook proxy** in section 5. AccountCore must already hold the account's trading funds; a trade uses internal balances rather than pulling from an external wallet each time.

Key entrypoints (overloads also exist):

```solidity
swap(uint40 userId, bool isBuy, uint128 amountIn, uint128 minAmountOut, uint64 deadline);
batch(uint40 userId, NativeOrder[] orders, uint8[] cancelSlotIdxs);
replaceBySlotPacked(uint40 userId, bytes packedOps);
cancelAllOrders(uint40 userId);
estimateSwap(uint40 userId, bool isBuy, uint128 amountIn);
getL2Book(uint256 levels);
bestBidAsk();
```

`swap` amounts use raw atoms; `deadline` is Unix seconds. `NativeOrder` is `(uint8 side,uint96 quantity,uint32 price,uint8 tif,uint8 executionInstruction,uint32 minSizeAfterBlock)`, with quantity/price precision from section 5. Side: BUY=0, SELL=1; TIF: GTC=0, IOC=1, FOK=2; execution instruction: NONE=0, POST_ONLY=1. `getL2Book(levels)` returns arrays padded with zeros to the requested depth, even for empty books. Use the ABI from the pinned source revision for overload selection and full tuple layouts.

The **KuruTradingWallet implementation** `0xa478b5a38aabDf8b31f0ec7443a274162214Cd18` provides EIP-7702 logic. Signed actions execute at each **delegated EOA's address and storage context**, not by treating the implementation as a user's funded wallet. The delegated EOA must have the necessary AccountCore TRADE authorization for the account. Direct trading and this signed-intent periphery are separate call paths.

Trading-wallet domain: `KuruTradingWallet`, version `2`, chain 143, verifying contract **the delegated EOA address**. Actions include batch/replace/cancel/FOK, triggers and TWAP. Use the exact intent schemas from the deployed revision. `maxFutureNonceSkewMillis = 60000` (60 seconds); wallet intent nonces have their own time semantics and must not be confused with withdrawal nonces or deadlines.

KeeperAuthority `0xbc36eC07800150489f9ED0f86a2d3E27Ca36980e` is bound to the trading-wallet implementation. Its owner is `0xfeb3BF5CE7A6b0A59bcc6cb8308661b45aCa002c` and pending owner is zero. No trading-keeper grants were made during this market deployment. Check `isKeeper(candidate)` before routing keeper actions; oracle updater permissions do not grant trading-wallet keeper permissions.

This reference does not establish that a separate trigger/TWAP execution service is running.

## 9. Oracle publisher status

**KEEPER1 is live on the six new manual sources.** Its target configuration matches the new AccountCore, WithdrawalLimiter and source addresses. Initial publications and subsequent heartbeats were confirmed after the cutover. The worker no longer publishes to the old sources. KEEPER2 is authorized but a second worker was not started by this deployment.

- Equities use Databento `EQUS.MINI` quotes during the regular US cash session, with the configured session calendar and 300-second cash-open blend. Premarket/postmarket quotes are not selected as cash-session prices.
- Outside the cash session, equities use the configured multi-venue perp pricing with a **300-second EWMA half-life** and live USD conversion.
- XAUt0 uses Binance and Bybit **XAUT spot** prices with live USDT/USD conversion, rather than treating spot gold/XAU as XAUT.
- Price inputs arrive through NATS; the direct Nasdaq halt checker remains the temporary status-source exception.

Configured publication scheduling: 60-second heartbeat, 20 bps deviation trigger and 10-second minimum interval, requiring valid fresh observations. These are scheduling targets, not guarantees during feed or chain failures. The service preserves source observation times.

After market deployment, all six assets were ready, no transaction was pending, and observed onchain ages were 5–58 seconds. This is a recorded health snapshot, not continuous-uptime certification. Gas funding and operational monitoring remain required. The service journals signed transactions before broadcast; do not run two processes with the same keeper wallet or discard a pending journal without reconciling its nonce and hash.
